question:
Error: "MBEANSTARTER LOADEXTENSIONS FAILED TO LOAD EXTENSION" occurs at portal startup We are using Portal Server 8.5 and when starting the Portal server we see following error:

0000005e MBeanStarter E com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.MBeanStarter loadExtensions failed to load extension: key: ServerExt.applications / value: com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions

How can we resolve this error?
answer:
A code fix for this issue is integrated into the WebSphere Portal & WCM Combined Cumulative Fix 06 (PI36060 [http://www-01.ibm.com/support/docview.wss?uid=swg1PI36060]) for Portal 8.5.0.0 available from Fix Central: http://www-933.ibm.com/support/fixcentral/swg/selectFixes?parent =ibm/WebSphere&product=ibm/WebSphere/WebSphere+Portal&release=Al l&platform=All&function=aparId&apars=PI36060

However, a temporary fix is also available:

LOCAL FIX * 
1) Open the WAS admin console. 
2) Navigate to Resources > Resource environment providers > WP ScriptingService > Custom properties. 
3) You should see an entry with the name "ServerExt.applications" and value "com.ibm.wps.scripting.server.ApplicationServerExtensions" 
4) Delete this entry, save, and restart the server.

question: Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? Why SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above? The same configuration works on v7.2.
answer:
The SSH connections fail after upgrade to v7.5.2 and above because the default set of ciphers and MACs has been altered to remove unsafe algorithms. In particular, CBC ciphers and arcfour* are disabled by default. The full set of algorithms remains available if configured explicitly via the Ciphers and MACs sshd_config options. 

This change was made to remove unsafe algorithms, which have security vulnerabilities. The upgrade to OpenSSH 6.9p1 was necessary in order to fix several published CVE vulnerabilities in the OpenSSH code and ensure security. 

In the case of DataPower Gateway version 7.5, the following algorithms were disabled by default:

- Disabled diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1 and diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 algorithms by default.
- Disabled MD5-based MAC algorithms.
- Limited DH-GEX to 4096 bits for Cisco devices.

To resolve the issue, you can either upgrade the SSH client/server to a version where it uses the safe algorithms in the default lists, or modify the OpenSSH configuration file to enable the legacy algorithms. However, the first option is recommended as it uses the secure algorithms and does not introduce back in unsafe algorithms.

question: Limitations of sylog-TCP log target using DataPower Gateways I am trying to configure a log target using type syslog-TCP. It seems that the payload is getting truncated when I try to record custom logs to it using log-action. Why is this? How can I workaround it.
answer:
The limitation of the syslog-TCP log target using DataPower Gateways is that it has a finite amount of space to hold larger than average log files or long term logging needs in production environment. This can cause log events to be dropped if the device is under high load. 

Additionally, the syslog protocol operates over UDP which has no guarantee on packet delivery - a fast fire and forget method. This can also cause log events to be dropped.

To workaround this issue, you can consider using a TCP-based method such as SOAP or Syslog-ng, which ensures packet delivery to the destination. You can also tune the Rate Limit setting to limit total connections from the log target.

It is also mentioned that log events dropped can be confirmed or counted from the Status>Log Targets menu in the WebGUI.
